subject: Request: Dedicated pool queueing exception & manual fallback — Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@nimbushealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool queueing behavior / exception request

Hi Vanessa,

Quick note from procurement and infra at Nimbus Health — we’re finalizing the Dedicated capacity purchase but have one open item from our SREs: they need an explicit carve-out for queueing behavior during batch ingest windows. The workload is predictable: nightly bulk inference (3–4 hour window, heavy concurrency spikes) that currently would violate the standard per-pool concurrency model and cause throttling by Redwood’s queueing policy.

What we need to confirm: is there a formal way to request an SLA variance so our Dedicated pool can be configured with: 
- guaranteed concurrent slot reservation for X GPUs during a scheduled window
- manual fallback routing to a pinned, higher-throughput variant with known latencies if queue depth exceeds threshold

We’re on a deadline to close the contract this month and this carve-out is blocking sign-off. Can you let us know next steps and whether Redwood will accept a short-term exception or needs a custom engineering change?

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Hayes
Head of Infrastructure, Nimbus Health

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll loop in our SRE lead (Jonas) and our Serving PM to confirm what we can do operationally without engine changes.
2) Please complete the attached SLA-variance-form (we received it, thanks). That will surface exact concurrency/sequence-length numbers which drive kernel selection and queueing behavior.
3) If the variance requires a manual fallback to a higher-throughput variant during the window, we may need a short runbook and approval for scheduled manual routing.

I’m copying Jonas for technical details — can you confirm the expected GPU count reservation during the 03:00–07:00 UTC window and the typical peak sequence lengths?

Best,

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool queueing behavior / exception request

Vanessa / Marcus — quick technical read: based on Oliver’s note, this looks like a scheduled spike that could be handled by two operational approaches, no kernel-level changes required if we accept a runbook: 

Option A — Reserved slot carve-out (preferred):
- Create a time-bound reservation that pins N concurrent slots on the customer’s reserved pool for the nightly window.
- Pros: predictable throughput, minimal routing complexity.
- Cons: reduces burst headroom for other customers on shared infra unless pool is fully dedicated (they’re buying Dedicated already).

Option B — Manual fallback + autoscale override:
- During the window, trigger a manual policy that routes overflow traffic to a pinned higher-throughput variant (quantized or compiled for lower latency) with temporary increased concurrency limits.
- Pros: better utilization outside the window.
- Cons: requires manual intervention or a scheduled automation; introduces a temporary divergence in latency SLOs and needs sign-off.

We need the following from Nimbus to size the reservation:
- exact GPU count to reserve (or % of pool),
- expected qps/token-rate and peak concurrent requests (for the 3–4 hour window),
- whether they require automatic failover or manual-runbook activation.

I can sketch the queueing diagram and expected latency curves if they share sample traces. Marcus, can you confirm if our current Dedicated control plane supports a time-window reservation config or if we need a short engineering task?

— Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 11:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool queueing behavior / exception request

Oliver / team — following up with specifics after a quick infra check. We do support scheduled reservation toggles for Dedicated pools via an ops API (internal flag). It’s not exposed in self-serve today but works for enterprise contracts with a short operational agreement.

What we can offer immediately (example parameters):
- Reservation: 8x A100-equivalent concurrent slots reserved for 03:00–07:00 UTC nightly, applied at the pool level.
- Fallback: overflow routed to a pinned variant (v-quant-higher-thru) with documented latency profile; routing is activated automatically once queue depth > 120 requests OR via a scheduled flag.
- SLAs: during the reserved window we provide throughput guarantees but latency SLOs will be relaxed for overflow requests routed to the fallback variant; any SLA credits will be scoped to capacity outages only (not to expected degraded latency during fallback).

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a queueing diagram and example runbook.

Action items for Nimbus:
- Confirm reservation size (GPU slots or absolute GPUs) and exact window (we can do cron-style schedule),
- Approve fallback routing behavior and the relaxed latency carve-out language (I’ll draft the short appendix).

If you approve, we’ll schedule a short runbook handoff with our ops team and document the exception in the contract appendix.

Marcus Lin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Oliver — thanks for the quick turnaround and sorry for the tight timeline. Recapping what Marcus proposed and the recommended next steps so procurement can close: 

Proposal summary (for contract appendix):
- Scheduled reservation: 8 GPU-equivalent concurrent slots reserved nightly 03:00–07:00 UTC (can be adjusted based on your numbers).
- Automated overflow routing: requests above queue depth 120 (or configured threshold) will be routed to a pinned higher-throughput variant; latency SLOs for overflow requests are relaxed and documented in the appendix.
- Operational runbook: Redwood ops will provide a 30-minute SLA to activate/deactivate reservations outside schedule in emergency scenarios.
- Term: trial carve-out for first 90 days, after which we’ll review usage and either codify into the standard Dedicated plan or revert.

Please reply with a single-line confirmation of: GPU count (8 ok?), window (03:00–07:00 UTC ok?), and approval to include relaxed latency language in the contract appendix. Once I have that I’ll attach the appendix draft and route to legal/procurement.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
